executive_summary: EUR/GBP trades at 0.85965 (payload spot, spotDate 2026-09-03), meaning one euro buys 0.85965 pounds; a rising pair is a stronger euro and a weaker pound. The pair has spent a year drifting the wrong way for a euro bull — down 1.10% over twelve months, 0.34% over six and 0.57% over three — and the last month is the first positive one in that sequence at +0.22%, with spot sitting at the 36th percentile of its 52-week closing range of 0.84671-0.88308. The dominant bilateral narrative is a scheduled compression of sterling's carry advantage: the differential is -150bp on identical 2.9% headline inflation in both economies, the ECB is roughly 97% priced to raise its deposit rate to 2.50% on 10 September, and the Bank of England on 17 September carries about +7bp with the market having pushed its next move into 2027. Two bilateral differentials diverge materially from the standalone dossier views — both currencies are net energy importers facing the same gas shock, but one absorbs it from a current-account surplus of 1.7% of GDP and the other from a 2.8% deficit; and the gilt-Bund spread at roughly 184bp is the widest since the 2022 mini-Budget, paid on the debt of the sovereign whose central bank is less likely to hike. Pass 1's settled verdict is Bullish at conviction 3 on both horizons, net weighted scores +0.3654 tactically and +0.4368 strategically, and the price payload arrived after that verdict was set — it neither confirms nor contradicts the direction, but it does show spot pressing a 200-week average it has closed below for nine consecutive weeks, with a 10-touch resistance band beginning only 18 pips overhead. Our one substantive caveat, which we publish rather than bury, is that a long position pays roughly 131bp a year on the payload's observed funding premium — about 9 pips a month against a 22-pip ATR — so the carry-adjusted risk/reward on a spot expression is materially worse than the score levels imply, and the conviction-3 call is far better carried in the option tenors that contain the 28 October Budget than in spot. The path of least resistance is a stepped advance through the 100-day at 0.86043 and the 200-day at 0.86533 toward the 11-touch 0.8706-0.8777 band, resolved in three dated windows: 15-17 September, 28 October, and 17 December.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no PPP series for this cross in either dossier, so valuation is a REER-relative proxy and must not be read as a fair-value level. On BIS real effective exchange rates for June 2026, the euro stands at 102.69 against sterling at 111.41, making the euro 8.49% cheaper than the pound in real effective terms; equalising the two indices would imply EUR/GBP near 0.9284, which is 3,187 pips above spot and is best understood as a statement about accumulated real appreciation rather than a target. Sterling's REER is the third-highest in the G10-plus-Singapore set behind the Australian and Singapore dollars, while the euro's sits fifth of eleven and has drifted 1.20 points lower over twelve months. Two valuation measures therefore point the same way without either being tactically actionable: the pair is at the 36th percentile of its own one-year distribution, and the euro is the cheap leg on the only trade-weighted measure available. What is priced in the current level is sterling's 150bp nominal carry advantage — which, because both economies printed 2.9% headline inflation in July, is also a 150bp real advantage and therefore genuine rather than an inflation artefact. What is not priced is the scheduled compression of that advantage.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Carry is against a long EUR/GBP position and it is the single largest argument for restraint in this report. On the policy basis the differential is -150bp (ECB deposit 2.25% vs Bank Rate 3.75%). On the observed basis, the payload's CME 6E/6B calendar-spread premium is +131.4bp annualised, which is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis and implies a benign basis of roughly -19bp, consistent with the -18bp 3-month EUR/USD basis and the roughly -12.5bp derived GBP/USD basis. The carry-to-vol ratio on the policy basis is -0.43; for comparison, the euro's best positive-carry cross earns +0.58 against the franc, so a long EUR/GBP position gives up roughly a full unit of risk-adjusted carry relative to the alternative expression. The 6-month outright of 0.8653 lands within 2 pips of the 200-day moving average, a coincidence worth noting. Carry is working against the position but the regime is improving from the euro's side for the first time in three years: a delivered 25bp ECB hike on 10 September cuts the policy-basis cost from 150bp to 125bp (~7.8 pips/month), and a plausible February 2027 configuration of ECB 2.75% against Bank Rate 3.50% would cut it to 75bp (~4.7 pips/month). The directional call therefore faces a hurdle that is real, measurable and shrinking, which is precisely why the expression matters as much as the direction.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral differential is -150bp: the ECB deposit rate is 2.25% against a Bank Rate of 3.75%, and because both economies printed 2.9% headline inflation in July the real differential is identical to the nominal one at -150bp. Sterling's carry advantage is therefore genuine rather than an artefact of inflation differentials, and that is the honest counterweight to this stance. What favours the pair is the direction of travel, not the level. OIS prices the ECB's 25bp move on 10 September at roughly 97%, taking the deficit to -125bp, while the Bank of England on 17 September has only about +7bp priced and 56 of 64 economists in the mid-August Reuters poll expect no change for the remainder of 2026; by 31 August the market had pushed the next BoE move into 2027 altogether. One leg moves and the other does not, so a sixth of sterling's carry advantage is mechanically removed inside four weeks. Both September outcomes are close to fully discounted, so the edge is not the events themselves but the asymmetry of the residual distributions: the euro's terminal is already priced at 2.75% by February 2027 with two-sided risk, whereas sterling's next move has been priced out entirely and the domestic data behind it lean one way. Transmission is unusually clean because the pair strips out the dollar leg completely, so neither the 16 September FOMC nor the dollar smile contaminates the bilateral read. The offsetting cost is carry: the payload's CME calendar-spread funding premium is +131.4bp annualised, so a long EUR/GBP position pays roughly that to hold, and three standing MPC hawks make a hawkish 17 September vote split a live squeeze risk.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the compression compounds. The euro's path is priced from 2.25% to 2.50% on 10 September and to 2.75% by early 2027; sterling's committee is split between three members who wanted 4.00% in July and a dovish wing whose leading voice describes an economy drifting toward deficient demand, with the base-currency dossier's own peer table carrying a 25bp BoE cut to 3.50% by February 2027 as its central case. If both paths deliver, the euro's deficit narrows from -150bp to -75bp, halving sterling's carry advantage inside the strategic horizon. The decision that would do it is dated: 5 November is the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Report round, the first full forecast after the 28 October Budget, and 17 December is the single highest-information bilateral date of the horizon because the ECB publishes new staff projections and the MPC decides on the same day. The market's own read of the July minutes is that the reaction function is genuinely symmetric, and with private-sector pay at 2.8% against a target-consistent estimate near 3.25%, the incoming evidence points to the dovish resolution. The risk running the other way is real and caps confidence in the fifties: the euro's 2.75% terminal has to be reconciled with a negotiated wage tracker at 2.1% for Q2 2026 and Eurosystem projections showing 2.0% inflation in 2028, so a downward repricing of the euro leg is at least as likely as an upward repricing of the sterling leg. Both legs carry dovish risk; the point is that sterling's is larger because sterling has more carry to lose and a fiscal event forcing the issue.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is close to zero and the growth differential marginally favours sterling, so the bullish case here rests entirely on the reaction functions rather than the levels. Euro-area July HICP was 2.9% headline with core at 2.5% and services at 3.3%; UK July CPI was also 2.9% with core at 2.6% and services at 3.4% and falling. On activity the UK is nominally ahead — GDP +1.2% year-on-year against +1.0%, August composite PMI 52.5 against 52.1 — so a naive growth-differential read would be bearish for the pair. What makes it bullish is that the same imported energy shock is hawkish for one central bank and explicitly look-through for the other. The euro area's surprise run has been on both legs simultaneously — Ifo, GfK, ESI and new orders all beating, with August country CPIs printing up — feeding a Governing Council that has already delivered a hike. In the UK the equivalent data are dividing against themselves: services CPI fell, input PPI missed hard, retail sales fell and the CBI distributive trades survey missed, while the Governor has argued the gilt curve is doing the tightening in place of a rate rise. So identical inflation prints translate into a hiking euro and a stationary pound, which is the bilateral transmission. Confidence is held at 52 because the level and growth comparisons genuinely favour sterling and the 16 September UK CPI carries a real upside skew from energy pass-through.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two inflation processes decompose differently and the labour markets diverge, and both work for the pair. The euro-area overshoot is imported: energy contributed +0.94pp of the 2.9% July headline at +10.0% year-on-year while food, alcohol and tobacco decelerated and non-energy industrial goods sit at 0.9% — a cost-push overshoot on a labour market with unemployment stable at 6.3% and negotiated wages at 2.1%. The UK overshoot is also imported, but it lands on a labour market that is visibly loosening: unemployment 4.9% and up 0.2pp on the year, payrolled employees down 210,000, vacancies at their lowest since early 2021, private-sector regular pay at 2.8% and real regular pay growth of only 0.5%, with the Decision Maker Panel showing year-ahead expected wage growth at 3.4%. The bilateral implication is that the UK is absorbing the energy shock through household real income and employment while the euro area absorbs it through margins, with euro-area selling-price expectations actually falling. A deficient-demand adjustment in the quote economy against a stabilising, fiscally-supported base economy narrows the growth gap in the euro's favour over the horizon and removes the sterling hawks' evidence base. Confidence is 54 rather than higher because the euro-area improvement is narrow, with German services and the French composite both in contraction.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Reduced at both horizons (-0.03 tactical, -0.02 strategic). EUR/GBP is the framework's canonical low-risk-beta cross: neither leg is a safe haven, neither is a high-beta commodity proxy, and both dossiers independently score risk appetite the same way and in the same direction for their own currency, so the bilateral content of the global risk cycle is close to nil. The weight is moved to Factor 8, where the bilateral differential is genuine.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The global risk regime is unambiguously benign — VIX at 14.51 on 27 August, down 3.70 points on the month and near the 2026 low, US investment-grade spreads at 79bp and high yield at 263bp and 21bp tighter, US equities at records — and it helps both legs of this pair in almost exactly the same way. The base dossier classifies the euro as a non-haven that benefits from the risk-neutral goldilocks zone; the quote dossier classifies sterling as mildly risk-positive with less beta than the Antipodeans. Both scored their own risk factor Bullish tactically at 55 and 53 respectively, which for the cross nets to nothing. The equity channel is the only place a differential appears and it points in two directions at once: the Euro Stoxx 50 set a record above 6,560 and the DAX above 26,450, while the FTSE 100 is up roughly 20% on the year but the domestically-exposed FTSE 250 has underperformed it by about 10 percentage points. So European large-cap leadership is a mild euro-positive portfolio channel while the UK's own domestic equity signal is weak — a real but small bilateral tilt that does not survive the weighting. There is no haven-versus-proxy asymmetry to exploit here, no commodity beta differential, and no cross-asset instrument whose move reliably resolves this pair. The honest output is Neutral scored on cross-asset evidence rather than a manufactured tilt.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both economies are net energy importers buying into the same supply shock, so this factor is not about who is hurt but about who can absorb it. The euro area absorbs it from a current-account surplus of 1.7% of GDP with a goods surplus of EUR282bn; the United Kingdom absorbs it from a current-account deficit of 2.8% of GDP with a goods deficit of 7.6% of GDP and a services surplus that actually fell GBP 1.2bn to GBP 51.8bn in the same quarter. That is a 4.5 percentage point differential in external position, and it is the whole factor. The price shock itself is common: Dutch TTF topped EUR70 per megawatt hour on 31 August, the highest since January 2023, while UK NBP settled at 161.02 pence per therm on 26 August against the Bank of England's own July conditioning assumption of 136 pence, an 18-21% overshoot, with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed. Crude cuts the other way for both equally, with Brent down 12.0% from its July peak to USD 88.24. Tactically the news flow has been mixed for the base leg — the euro area posted a EUR35.1bn June current-account surplus against a EUR26.8bn forecast — and unambiguously negative for the quote leg, whose Q1 trade deficit widened GBP 5.1bn. The bilateral trade relationship reinforces: on IMF DOTS the euro area ran a USD 153.6bn goods surplus with the UK in 2024, a standing commercial requirement to sell sterling for euros.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 strategic weight this is the second-largest factor and the most durable bullish leg in the analysis. Both dossiers independently reach a Bearish external-balance stance for their own currency, at 66 and 63 confidence respectively, which for the cross resolves to whichever balance sheet degrades faster — and that is unambiguously sterling's. The euro area's twelve-month surplus has fallen from 2.0% to 1.7% of GDP, driven by a EUR60bn fall in the goods surplus, but it remains a surplus that finances itself. The UK is running a 2.8% deficit whose goods component is widening while the services surplus that historically offsets it is shrinking, and the headline Q1 narrowing came entirely from a GBP 8.0bn primary-income swing rather than from trade. The forward constraint tightens for both: EU storage at 62.99% on 24 August is well below average with Goldman Sachs saying explicitly that current prices will not be enough to manage storage through winter and that December TTF may need to exceed EUR100 per megawatt hour, and UK NBP is already 18-21% above the Bank's own assumption with the northern heating season inside the horizon. Net, the winter is bad for both and worse for the one that must attract foreign financing to pay for it. The structural bilateral flow adds a floor: a USD 153.6bn euro-area goods surplus with the UK is a persistent sterling-selling requirement, and post-Brexit trade frictions have reduced UK trade openness rather than raised it. Confidence is 62 rather than higher because a Hormuz reopening would collapse both bills at once and would take the euro's rate story with it.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: The euro area is the world's largest net energy importer and its critical commodity is European natural gas: Dutch TTF above EUR70 per megawatt hour on 31 August, the highest since January 2023, with EU storage 62.99% full on 24 August and energy contributing +0.94pp of the 2.9% July HICP at +10.0% year-on-year. It is also a net crude importer, so Brent's 12.0% decline from its July peak is a partial offset. It carries no commodity export offset of consequence.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: The United Kingdom is likewise a net energy importer with no commodity export offset. Its critical price is UK NBP gas, which settled at 161.02 pence per therm on 26 August and traded around 165 pence on 28 August against the Bank of England's own July conditioning assumption of 136 pence, an 18-21% overshoot with a twelve-month change of roughly +43%. Brent's decline is the same partial offset it is for the euro area.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: The framework's direction rules give natural gas up as negative for both EUR and GBP, and oil up as negative for both, so a naive netting produces zero. Netting on price alone is the wrong operation here; the netting must be on absorptive capacity, because the shock is common and the balance sheets are not. Step one: TTF and NBP are cointegrated through interconnector flows and competition for the same marginal LNG cargo, so the two legs face effectively the same percentage shock. Step two: the euro area absorbs it from a current-account surplus of 1.7% of GDP with a EUR282bn goods surplus; the UK absorbs it from a 2.8%-of-GDP deficit with a goods deficit of 7.6% of GDP and a services surplus that fell GBP 1.2bn in the same quarter — a 4.5 percentage point differential in external position. Step three: a surplus economy pays a larger import bill out of its own net earnings, while a deficit economy must attract incremental foreign financing to pay it, and that financing requirement is what shows up in the currency. Step four: crude's 12% decline is common and roughly symmetric and therefore nets out, leaving gas as the only commodity term with bilateral content. Conclusion: European gas up is mildly BULLISH EUR/GBP, and the effect scales with the level of gas rather than with its direction alone.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Mildly bullish EUR/GBP, and smaller than the gas term. Brent up 10% raises both import bills; neither currency has an export offset, so the differential runs through absorptive capacity and favours the surplus economy. Second-order: it firms the ECB's hiking impulse more than the BoE's, because the Governing Council has said it will act against the energy shock while the Bank has said it will look through it.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Mildly bearish EUR/GBP. Both import bills improve, relieving the deficit economy proportionately more in cash terms, and — more importantly — a sustained crude decline erodes the inflation impulse that is the euro leg's entire rate story, which is exactly the mechanism by which the market pushed the next BoE move to 2027 after Brent fell 12% from its July peak. A crude collapse is the cleanest way for this pair's bull case to fail.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: European natural gas — TTF for the base leg and NBP for the quote leg, which are effectively the same price expressed in two units. The pair's exposure is not to the level of gas but to the differential in balance-sheet capacity to absorb it, which is why the same shock that hurts both currencies against the dollar is mildly positive for EUR/GBP.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance divergence is wide and the sequencing favours the base leg. The Account of the ECB's 22-23 July meeting, published 27 August, twice described the hold as a pause and stated it was important not to signal the end of the tightening cycle, judging a further increase likely unless the inflation outlook improved significantly — and the market moved to roughly 97% for 10 September within days. The Bank of England's 29 July communication is the opposite in kind rather than merely in degree: a 6-3 hold in which the majority's stated rationale was that holding, combined with the tightening of financial conditions since the conflict began, was providing sufficient insurance, with the Governor citing the upward-sloping yield curve as doing some of the work. Ramsden gave explicitly two-way guidance and Taylor argued the economy is drifting toward deficient demand. Sequencing matters mechanically here: the ECB decides on 10 September with new staff projections and the MPC follows on 17 September, so the base leg sets the tone and does so at the higher-signal meeting of the two. With euro-area energy at +10.0% year-on-year and August country CPIs surprising up, an upward revision to the 2026 and 2027 inflation paths from the June baseline of 3.0% and 2.3% is likely and would read hawkish. The tactical risk is tonal rather than structural: if the ECB President repeats the July acknowledgement that there is no clear evidence of second-round effects while delivering the hike, the pair sells the fact.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically both central banks are credible and both risk being repriced dovishly, which genuinely offsets. The ECB has executed a difficult sequence cleanly — identified an energy shock, said it would act, acted on 11 June, then paused without letting the market conclude the cycle was over — but the market has extrapolated that to a 2.75% terminal by early 2027 which has to be reconciled with the Bank's own negotiated wage tracker at 2.1% for Q2 2026 and its own June projections showing 2.0% inflation in 2028. The base dossier's own view is that the euro terminal is 15-25bp too high, and the vehicle for that repricing is dated: the 17 December projections round, the first vintage in which 2026 energy base effects come clearly into the 2027 and 2028 forecast window. The Bank of England's reaction function is symmetric rather than mis-specified, with three standing hawks against a dovish wing and a decisive input — 2027 pay settlements — that the Committee itself expects to learn about toward the end of this year, placing the resolution at 5 November and 17 December. So both legs face a dovish repricing risk at the same two dates, and 17 December carries both simultaneously. The differential is that the sterling repricing would be larger in basis points because sterling has more to give up, but the euro repricing would be larger in surprise terms because the euro's hawkish extrapolation is the more extended of the two. Two credible banks with opposite-signed extrapolation risks at the same dates is a Neutral, and at a 0.12 weight that costs the score nothing rather than manufacturing a tilt.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The gilt-Bund 10-year spread stands at approximately 184bp — gilt 5.16% at the 28 August close against a Bund of 3.32% on 31 August — which is the widest since the 2022 mini-Budget and, critically, is being paid on the debt of the sovereign whose central bank is less likely to raise rates than the other. Because Bank Rate is only 12.5bp above the Fed midpoint while gilts yield 49bp over Treasuries, the decomposition is unambiguous: a large part of the sterling long-end premium is term and fiscal premium rather than policy. The 30-year gilt at 5.73-5.76% sits within 5bp of its May 2026 multi-decade peak. On the base side the comparable spreads are contained and improving in character: OAT-Bund 83.6bp, BTP-Bund roughly 81-85bp, and Germany is expanding fiscally with new borrowing above EUR180bn and a EUR500bn infrastructure fund while its own 10-year sits at a fifteen-year high without any widening of peripheral spreads. Higher core yields with contained peripheral spreads is genuine term-premium repricing; higher gilt yields with a 184bp premium over the core is a credit-perception repricing. The bilateral transmission runs two ways and both favour the pair: the fiscal premium substitutes for a Bank Rate rise, as the Governor has said in as many words, and the quote dossier's regime-dependent correlation says a rising long gilt yield sells sterling once the fiscal regime binds. Tactically there is no dated catalyst, which is why confidence is 58 rather than higher, but the spread has refused to narrow ahead of a Budget, and refusal is itself information.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: This is the highest-confidence stance in the analysis because the arithmetic is closed and adverse on one side and genuinely two-sided on the other. UK public sector net debt is 95.1% of GDP, the highest since the early 1960s, the OBR's March headroom of GBP 9.9bn has plausibly been consumed entirely by the intervening rise in gilt yields at roughly GBP 2.5bn of debt service per 0.25 percentage point, and the resolution is dated at 28 October with three options — tax rises, spending cuts or a rule change — the last of which the gilt market will not tolerate. The euro area's fiscal picture is genuinely two-sided rather than merely better: a AAA Germany borrowing heavily against an A+ France unable to consolidate, with the fat left tail located in Paris rather than Rome and the base dossier's own central risk case an OAT-Bund move beyond 110-120bp during the autumn budget process. But the euro area has no single sovereign, so a French widening is diluted, whereas a gilt event is the whole currency. That structural difference — a concentrated single-sovereign exposure against a mutualised distribution of exposures — is the bilateral content, and it is why the pair benefits even in a scenario where both fiscal stories deteriorate. tactical.rationale: At the applied tactical weights, 45% of the signal sits with Policy & Rates and Inflation & Growth, and both point the same way for the same underlying reason. The bilateral differential is -150bp, and because the euro area and the United Kingdom both printed 2.9% headline inflation in July, the real differential is also -150bp — sterling's carry advantage is genuine, not an inflation artefact, and that is the honest starting point. What favours the pair is not the level but the trajectory and the reaction functions. OIS has the ECB at roughly 97% for 25bp on 10 September, taking the deficit to -125bp, while the Bank of England on 17 September has about +7bp priced, 56 of 64 economists expect no change all year, and the market has pushed the next BoE move into 2027 altogether. One leg moves and the other does not. The deeper bilateral mechanism is that the same imported energy shock is hawkish for one central bank and explicitly look-through for the other: the July ECB Account described the hold twice as a pause and judged a further hike likely, while the July MPC minutes had the majority arguing that tightened financial conditions were providing sufficient insurance and the Governor citing the upward-sloping yield curve as doing some of the work. Identical inflation, opposite policy consequences. The two standalone dossiers reinforce rather than conflict: euro Bullish at conviction 2 and ranked 3 of 11, sterling Bearish at conviction 2 and ranked 8 of 11, and the sterling dossier's own bearish case is built partly on the ECB hiking — a direct read-through to this cross. The bilateral factors that modify the standalone views are the external balance and the sovereign premium. Both economies are net energy importers facing the same shock, but one absorbs it from a 1.7%-of-GDP current-account surplus and the other from a 2.8% deficit whose goods component is widening while its services offset shrinks, and the euro area runs a USD 153.6bn goods surplus with the UK that is a standing sterling-selling requirement. Meanwhile the gilt-Bund spread at roughly 184bp is the widest since the 2022 mini-Budget and is a premium paid on the debt of the country less likely to raise rates, against contained OAT-Bund at 83.6bp and BTP-Bund near 81-85bp. What is priced is both September decisions and a stable -125bp deficit thereafter; what is not priced is the asymmetry of the residual distributions, with sterling's next move priced out entirely while its own labour data — private-sector pay at 2.8%, unemployment at 4.9% and rising, vacancies at a five-year low — lean one way. The path of least resistance is a grind higher, front-loaded into 15-17 September when UK labour data, CPI and the MPC vote split arrive in three days. Dated catalysts: ECB with projections 10 September, UK labour market 15 September, UK CPI 16 September, MPC and the annual gilt-reduction vote 17 September, euro-area current account 18 September. Conviction is 3 rather than 4 for three specific reasons: a long position pays roughly 131bp a year on the payload's observed funding premium, three standing MPC hawks make a 5-4 vote split a live squeeze risk, and no single factor here clears 58 confidence.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework moves weight out of Inflation & Growth and Risk Appetite and into External Balance, Guidance and — as adjusted here — Fiscal and Event Risk, and every one of those reallocations lands where the bilateral differential is genuine. Policy & Rates remains the largest factor and stays Bullish because the compression compounds: the euro's path is priced from 2.25% to 2.75% by early 2027 while sterling's committee is split, its next move has been priced out to 2027, and the base dossier's own peer table carries a Bank Rate cut to 3.50% as its central case — a configuration that would narrow the deficit from -150bp to -75bp and halve sterling's carry advantage. The decisions that would do it are dated: 5 November is the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Report round and the first full forecast after the Budget, and 17 December carries an ECB projections round and an MPC decision on the same day, which makes it the single highest-information bilateral date of the horizon. External Balance is the second-largest weight and the most durable leg. Both dossiers independently reach a Bearish external stance for their own currency, so the cross resolves to whichever balance sheet degrades faster, and that is unambiguously sterling's: a 2.8%-of-GDP deficit with a goods deficit at 7.6% of GDP and a shrinking services offset, against a euro-area surplus of 1.7% that finances itself, with both facing the same winter gas path and Goldman Sachs warning that December TTF may need to exceed EUR100 per megawatt hour. Fiscal & Sovereign Risk is the highest-confidence stance in the analysis at 66, because the arithmetic is closed on one side: UK net debt at 95.1% of GDP, the OBR's March GBP 9.9bn of headroom plausibly consumed by the intervening rise in yields at roughly GBP 2.5bn per 0.25 percentage point, a 30-year gilt within 5bp of a multi-decade peak, and a resolution dated 28 October. The euro area's fiscal picture is genuinely two-sided — a heavily-borrowing AAA Germany against an A+ France unable to consolidate — but it is mutualised across twenty-plus sovereigns, whereas a gilt event is the whole currency. The factors compound rather than cancel: the energy shock keeps euro-area inflation high enough to justify the ECB while transferring UK national income abroad and worsening the fiscal arithmetic through inflation-linked spending, and every leg of that chain terminates at the Budget. What is priced against what we expect gives the edge: bank research on this pair — ING toward 0.870, Rabobank at 0.87 in three months, MUFG at 0.88 for Q4 — rests almost entirely on BoE hike expectations unwinding and Budget risk, and we could find no bank forecast that separately prices the terms-of-trade channel as an additive negative for a deficit economy. The path of least resistance is higher in two legs, September policy compression and an October-November fiscal and pay-data resolution, with the November-December heating peak testing both economies. Conviction is 3 rather than 4 because a Hormuz reopening at a plausible probability would remove the largest positive and the rate story together, and because a long position pays roughly 66bp of carry over six months.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic path is a stepped advance punctuated by two event windows and one seasonal test, not a trend. Expect the autumn to trade 0.8600-0.8700 as the September policy compression is banked and the market's attention rotates from the differential — which is settled for at least six weeks once the ECB and MPC have decided — to the fiscal calendar; the 10-touch 0.86140-0.86902 band should be worked through in two or three attempts rather than cleared in one, because its members cluster around the 100-day and 200-day averages and the bearish daily stack means systematic capital is not helping. The largest single repricing window is the fortnight around 28 October, where the Budget and its OBR forecast either validate or discharge a 184bp gilt-Bund premium; we expect a 100-200 pip move, direction dependent, and this is the window in which the position is made or lost. The largest pullback risk is the 5 November Monetary Policy Report, where three standing hawks vote again — a hike there would be worth 150-200 pips of squeeze and would likely retest the 200-week average at 0.85947 from above. From there the path depends on the winter gas balance and the 17 December double decision, which resolves both banks' extrapolations on the same day; a confirmed dovish sterling resolution carries the pair into the 11-touch 0.87060-0.87770 band, and clearing that band's upper edge is what would make the upside case live. Pattern shape: a broad stepped advance with a fat left tail located at 5 November and a fat right tail located at 28 October. Realised volatility should rise from 2.97% on a 60-day basis toward and above the 3.458% currently implied at 94.7 days, which we regard as too cheap for a horizon containing a Budget, a Monetary Policy Report and a heating season.

consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: Directionally aligned with the bullish bank cluster, roughly in line with the 0.87 three-month cluster at the short end, and modestly above the survey median at both horizons — while remaining well below the 0.88-0.90 2027 cluster and well above the Bank of America sterling-bull case
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: +67 pips above the Q3 survey median implied by a GBP/EUR median of 1.163 at 1M; +68 pips above the survey's early-2027 path of 0.8692 at 6M
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: The reasoning gap matters more than the level gap, because it determines what would falsify the call. The bullish houses get to 0.87 essentially through the rate channel — sterling's front-end support being pared back and BoE hike bets fading — which is our Factor 1, weighted heavily but not exclusively. Our additional leg, and the one we cannot find priced anywhere, is Factor 5 at a 0.16 strategic weight: the same winter energy shock hits both economies, but one absorbs it from a 1.7%-of-GDP current-account surplus and the other must attract incremental foreign financing to pay for it from a 2.8% deficit whose goods component is widening and whose services offset is shrinking, on top of a USD 153.6bn euro-area goods surplus with the UK that is a standing commercial requirement to sell sterling. We also weight Factor 8 at 0.11 strategically against a 0.07 default, and pass-2 research strengthens that choice: the substitutability asymmetry — that a French fiscal problem can be expressed within the single currency while a UK one cannot — is a bilateral flow mechanism, not a spread observation. Against the sterling bulls we differ on durability rather than on the existence of the carry: it is genuine in real terms today and it is a shrinking asset with three dated resolution points.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Roughly +164 pips or +1.90% on the strategic base case, +107 pips against the 6-month forward, and a position that survives outcomes which would break a pure rate call — a hawkish 17 September vote split or a 5 November hike would remove the rate leg while leaving the external-balance and fiscal legs intact.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: The most dangerous counter-argument is the contrarian positioning case: with the institutional community braced for trouble, a fiscally neutral Budget on 28 October would dissolve the remaining sterling risk premium, positioning would work in sterling's favour, and the event asymmetry would favour the pound — which maps directly onto our downside scenario. The second route to being wrong is a durable Hormuz reopening, which would relieve the UK import bill and remove the ECB's hiking impulse simultaneously, taking out the largest and second-largest positives at once. The third and nearest is a hot 16 September UK CPI plus a 5-4 MPC split, forcing a 2026 hike back into pricing against a fast-money community already positioned short this cross.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Both horizons are Bullish at conviction 3, and the thesis broadens rather than merely persists: the score deepens from +0.3654 to +0.4368 and overall confidence rises from 57% to 60%. The composition changes in an informative way. Tactically the case rests on five moderate-confidence positives of which policy and the data pulse supply two-thirds, with five honest zeros. Strategically the framework reallocates weight into External Balance and Fiscal and Event Risk, which is exactly where sterling's structural problems sit, so six factors contribute and the largest single positive is no longer policy alone. Two factors change character: Flows turns from Neutral to Bullish because the covering flow that currently bids sterling exhausts while a fast-money sterling long becomes the exposed position into a fiscal binary, and Guidance turns from Bullish to Neutral because both central banks' hawkish framings are extended in opposite directions and both get tested on the same two dates.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Because the volatility term structure slopes only 0.46 points from 38.6 to 185.7 days, the calendar is cheap relative to the carry. Express the tactical view in spot, in short event-defined exposure sized to a 48-pip stop below the 50-day at 0.85546, and express the strategic view in the 94.7-day and 185.7-day option tenors rather than by holding spot for six months and paying 56 pips to do it. A position that must span both horizons should be structured so that the September gains are banked and the Budget exposure is re-established in optionality.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections
catalysts.rationale: The base leg's decisive scheduled event and the first of the two September decisions, so it sets the tone seven days before the MPC. A 25bp move to a 2.50% deposit rate is priced at roughly 97%, mechanically narrowing the bilateral deficit from -150bp to -125bp; the decision itself is therefore not the catalyst, the projections are. With euro-area energy at +10.0% year-on-year and August country CPIs surprising up, an upward revision to the June baseline of 3.0% for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027 would read hawkish and extend the differential compression into December. The tactical risk is tonal: a repeat of the July acknowledgement of no clear evidence of second-round effects, delivered alongside the hike, would produce a sell-the-fact reaction.

catalysts.event: UK labour market report: unemployment, claimant count, average weekly earnings
catalysts.rationale: The single most informative release for the quote leg inside the tactical window, because the MPC has named pay as the variable that decides whether its hawkish tail survives. The prior prints were unemployment 4.9% and up 0.2pp on the year, private-sector regular pay only 2.8%, payrolled employees down 210,000 and vacancies at 705,000, the lowest since early 2021. A further loosening removes the second-round-effects case that supports sterling's 150bp advantage, which is the direct bilateral channel; a re-acceleration above 3.2% would revive it and is the clearest near-term risk to a long position in the pair.

catalysts.event: UK August CPI, core CPI and services CPI
catalysts.rationale: Genuinely two-sided for the pair and the reason the tactical inflation factor is only modestly bullish. July printed 2.9% headline with core at 2.6% and services falling to 3.4%, and August carries real upside risk from energy pass-through with NBP gas 18-21% above the Bank's own July conditioning assumption and shop-price inflation at a two-year high of 1.5%. A hot print revives a 2026 Bank Rate rise and squeezes the pair lower against a fast-money community already positioned short it; a soft print confirms the disinflation the majority relies on and pushes the next move further out, compressing the differential further.

catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision and minutes, plus the annual vote on the next twelve-month gilt reduction pace
catalysts.rationale: The rate outcome is close to fully discounted at roughly +7bp with 56 of 64 economists expecting no change all year, so the bilateral information is in the vote split and the quantitative tightening decision. A split softening from 6-3 toward 7-2 removes the hawkish tail that underwrites sterling's carry advantage a week after the ECB has raised its own rate, which is the cleanest possible sequencing for the pair. The gilt-reduction vote cuts the other way: a slower pace against a GBP 491bn APF stock and a 30-year yield near a multi-decade peak would be gilt-supportive and mildly sterling-supportive, and it is not priced.

catalysts.event: Euro-area monthly balance of payments (current account)
catalysts.rationale: The highest-information release of the month for the base leg's side of the strategic external-balance thesis. It shows whether June's EUR35.1bn surplus was a one-off or whether the erosion of the goods surplus from EUR342bn to EUR282bn is continuing under the energy shock. A further deterioration narrows the 4.5 percentage point external-position gap that is the whole content of Factor 5, and is therefore bearish for the pair even though the quote leg's own balance is worse; a stabilisation confirms that a surplus economy can fund the winter out of its own earnings while a deficit economy cannot.

catalysts.event: UK Autumn Budget with accompanying OBR economic and fiscal forecast
catalysts.rationale: The single most consequential dated event of the strategic horizon and the only one-sided binary either leg carries. A Chancellor three months in office must satisfy a fiscal mandate whose March headroom of GBP 9.9bn the OBR warned could be erased by a modest rise in borrowing costs, at roughly GBP 2.5bn of additional annual debt service per 0.25 percentage point, with the gilt-Bund spread already at 184bp and the 30-year within 5bp of a multi-decade peak. The distribution is asymmetric for the pair because the fiscal rules cap the good outcome while the gilt market punishes the bad one, and the quote leg's regime-dependent correlation turns a rising long yield into currency weakness once the fiscal regime binds.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision (no staff projections)
catalysts.rationale: A non-projection meeting six weeks after the September move and the day after the UK Budget, which makes the sequencing unusually informative for the pair: the market will read the euro leg's guidance immediately after having repriced the sterling leg's fiscal risk. The base case is a hold at 2.50%, so the language carries the content. A hold framed as another pause sustains the priced 2.75% terminal and the compression thesis; a hold framed as data-dependent with softer wage commentary begins the downward euro repricing that is the principal internal risk to this analysis.

catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision with Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The first full forecast round after the Budget and the meeting at which three standing hawks vote again with 2027 pay-settlement evidence beginning to arrive. It is the single largest squeeze risk to a long position in the pair: a rise to 4.00% would restore the differential toward -150bp or wider and would validate the sterling bulls. Equally, a vote softening toward 8-1 with a downgraded forecast would remove the hawkish tail entirely and confirm the dovish resolution the labour data point to. Because the Monetary Policy Report conditions its forecasts on market-implied rates, its published inflation path is an implicit verdict on the market's 2027 timing.

catalysts.event: Northern-hemisphere heating season peak (week-of, no fixed date): the physical test of EU storage at 62.99% and UK NBP at 18-21% above the Bank of England's conditioning assumption
catalysts.rationale: The highest-information non-scheduled event of the horizon and the mechanism through which Factor 5 pays or fails. Both economies are net energy importers facing the same price with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, and Goldman Sachs has said current prices will not be enough for Europe to manage storage through winter with December TTF possibly needing to exceed EUR100 per megawatt hour. The bilateral effect is not the price but the absorption: a surplus economy pays a larger bill out of net earnings while a 2.8%-of-GDP deficit economy must attract incremental financing, which is the channel that moves the pair.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council with new staff projections AND Bank of England MPC decision, on the same day
catalysts.rationale: The single highest-information bilateral date of the horizon, because both legs reprice simultaneously and one of them does so at a projections round. For the base leg it is the first vintage in which 2026 energy base effects come clearly into the 2027 and 2028 forecast window, and a downward revision would undermine the priced 2.75% terminal. For the quote leg it is the meeting at which the Committee expects to have learned about 2027 pay settlements, the input the July minutes named as decisive. Both banks' hawkish extrapolations are extended in opposite directions and both are tested here, which is precisely why the strategic guidance factor is scored Neutral.

catalysts.event: CFTC Commitments of Traders release for both legs, plus ECB Chief Economist remarks before the quiet period
catalysts.rationale: The first read on whether the two offsetting positioning flows that make Factor 4 tactically Neutral are still running: euro shorts covered 22,736 contracts in the week to 25 August and sterling shorts have covered roughly 10,100 a week for six weeks, and the disaggregated tranches used here are 21 days stale. Confirmation that leveraged funds remain short euro and long sterling would sharpen the contrarian read for the pair; further sterling covering would confirm the live bid against it. The ECB remarks are the last significant base-leg communication before the quiet period and the most likely vehicle for a late steer on 10 September.

catalysts.event: US-Iran conflict and the status of the Strait of Hormuz, monitored continuously (ongoing)
catalysts.rationale: The highest-impact and least predictable input, and genuinely two-sided for this pair rather than merely uncertain. Escalation raises both economies' energy bills and is mildly bullish for the pair through the absorptive-capacity channel, since a deficit economy must finance the increment while a surplus economy pays it from earnings. A durable ceasefire and reopening would collapse both bills and is the specific way this analysis is wrong: it relieves the quote leg's import bill and inflation problem while removing the base leg's hiking impulse, taking out the largest and second-largest positives at once. Nothing in the pair's volatility surface prices either branch.

assumptions: This is pass 2 of 2. The ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weight adjustments, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, G10 rankings, contrarian analyses, net commodity exposure and expression assessment are carried verbatim from the settled pass-1 verdict, scored without the price payload; nothing re-scores a factor because the chart agrees or disagrees.

The payload supplied dataPoints: 130 weekday bars, dateRange 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, spot 0.85965 at spotDate 2026-09-03, weekendBarsDropped: 0. Moving averages, support/resistance zones, 52-week ranges and 200-week figures are computed over the whole stored history (2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03, 4879 weekday bars), not the 130 visible bars.

Payload spot is dated 2026-09-03 while VALUATION_DATE is 2026-09-01, a two-session gap; every level, target, stop, pip calculation and distance-to-average is computed against the payload spot of 0.85965, disclosed rather than reconciled.

EUR/GBP is pounds per euro, EUR base and GBP quote; rising = euro stronger, sterling weaker. A bearish standalone sterling view is a BULLISH input for this pair, stated explicitly rather than left implicit.

Implied volatility is an estimate and a floor: EUR/GBP has no listed option, so the payload's surface is derived from the variance identity fed a realised correlation of 0.8371, disclosed as understating a direct Eurex quote by 8.7% on 2026-08-21 and running about 14% low in median across pairs. The carry-to-vol ratio inherits that estimate status.

Carry and forwards are derived, not quoted: the policy-basis differential is -150bp; the observed basis is -131.4bp from the payload's CME 6E/6B calendar-spread premium, which is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis; no quoted EUR/GBP forward-points source was obtainable, so the 1M/3M/6M outrights are computed linearly from that premium.

Both legs' 10-year sovereign yields in the payload are MONTHLY series as of 2026-06-01, 92 days old at valuation and outside both freshness windows; used only for the -182.6bp differential and never presented as live levels. Live gilt/Bund levels come from the dossiers with their own dates, and the resulting ~184bp spread is a cross-date approximation flagged as such (31 August was a UK bank holiday).
Bilateral trade figures are taken verbatim from the supplied IMF DOTS block (2024 goods, USD) and were not re-estimated from the web.

Valuation methodology uses BIS REER levels for June 2026 as a relative real-valuation proxy in the absence of any PPP series; the implied 0.9284 equalisation level is explicitly not a purchasing-power fair value.

Two different CFTC taxonomies appear and are not interchangeable: legacy non-commercial nets (25 August report date) versus Traders in Financial Futures disaggregated tranches (11 August, 21 days stale); both are labelled at every point of use.

Weight adjustments: five factors were adjusted, each within the ±0.05 limit, and both tactical and strategic sets sum to exactly 1.00 (Tactical: F1 +0.03, F8 +0.04, F3 -0.03, F10 -0.04; Strategic: F8 +0.04, F7 +0.02, F3 -0.02, F10 -0.04).

Net stance derivation was mechanical against the framework's stated thresholds (>=+0.10 Bullish, <=-0.10 Bearish, else Neutral); conviction and overall confidence remain judgements set below what the score levels alone might suggest.

Documented gaps, not filled: the 25-delta risk reversal, the pair's one-year implied-volatility percentile, EUR/GBP option barrier and strike-expiry data, and a quoted EUR/GBP cross-currency basis/forward-points series were all unobtainable and are recorded as gaps rather than estimated.

Chart-pattern sourcing is the one technical input the framework permits web research to supply; conflicting triangle and falling-channel readings are both reported rather than one being selected, and support/resistance levels were not web-searched but come entirely from the payload's computed clusters.
Consensus sourcing is via a survey aggregator and house-commentary summaries rather than a paid consensus feed; algorithmic/retail extrapolation sites were excluded as a category error.
Citation numbering: entries 1-28 are carried from the settled pass-1 verdict so references inside verbatim factor blocks remain valid; entries 29-41 are pass-2 bilateral research sources.
